chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) narrated that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down an angel to the earth. So that angel walked until he came to a door where a man was seeking permission from the owner of the house. The angel said to him: 'What is your need to the owner of this house?' He said: 'A Muslim brother of mine, whom I visited for the sake of Allah, Blessed and High'.

The angel said to him: 'Did nothing bring you except that?' He said: 'Nothing brought me except that.' He said: 'I am a messenger of Allah to you, and He conveys greetings to you and says: Paradise is obligated for you'.
And the angel said: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Whoever visits a Muslim, it is not him that he is visiting, but he is visiting Me, and his reward upon Me is Paradise'.

key_terms.زُرْتُهُ فِي اللَّهِ: visited him for the sake of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a Muslim brother for the sake of Allah?
ai.summary: In this renowned hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a divine encounter where an angel conveys Allah's promise of Paradise to a believer who visited his brother solely for Allah's sake. This narration underscores the Shia concept of *Ziyarat* (visitation) not merely as a social act but as a spiritual connection to the Divine, emphasizing that the reward is directly guaranteed by Allah. It highlights the theological significance of brotherhood in faith as a means of attaining closeness to God.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar Al Yamani, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> narrated to me<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> that Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sent an Angel down to the earth. So the Angel went walking until he came to a door at which was a man seeking permission from the owner of the house. So the Angel said to him: ‘What is your need to the owner of this house?’ He said, ‘A Muslim brother of mine whom I am visiting for the Sake of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Blessed and High’.

The Angel said to him: ‘You did not come for anything except for that?’ So he said, ‘I did not come for anything except for that’. So he said: ‘I am a messenger of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> to you and He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Conveys the Greetings to you and is Saying: “The Paradise is Obligated for you”.

And the Angel said ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying: “Whichever Muslim visits a Muslim, so it is not him that he is visiting, he is visiting Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and his Reward upon Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is the Paradise”’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yamani from Jabir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Jibril spoke to me that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, sent an angel to earth and the angel began walking until he came to a door where a man was asking for permission from the people of the house. The angel asked him, ‘What do you need from the owner of this house?’ He replied, ‘He is a Muslim brother (in belief). I have come to visit him for the sake of Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High.’

The angel then asked, ‘Is that the only reason for your visit?’ The man said, ‘Nothing else has brought me here but that.’ The angel then said, ‘I am the Messenger of Allah to you and He sends you the greeting of peace and says, ‘I have made paradise obligatory for you.’

The angel then said, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, says, ‘Whoever of the Muslims visits an other Muslim, in fact, has not visited him but he has visited Me and his reward from Me is paradise.’”
